```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# All analysis code is kept visible in the final document.  The runner writes
# compact, portable results so this report never has to materialise the H5AD.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5)
library(ggplot2)
library(mclust)
result_dir <- params$result_dir
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(result_dir, "domain_metadata.rds")))
result <- readRDS(file.path(result_dir, "domain_metadata.rds"))
model <- readRDS(file.path(result_dir, "torch_gmm_k20.rds"))
```

# Purpose and scope

This reproduces the post-representation spatial-domain stage of the official
CellCharter CosMx NSCLC analysis (He *et al.* data).  The official analysis
uses a supplied 10-dimensional scVI embedding; this R workflow deliberately
uses that representation only as an input, rebuilds a Delaunay graph separately
for every CosMx section, removes its longest 1% of edges, computes three-hop
neighbourhood features in R, and fits a full-covariance 20-component GMM using
R Torch.  This is therefore an honest check of R-native spatial aggregation and
clustering, not a claim that it reproduces Python labels byte-for-byte.

```{r model-summary}
data.frame(
  cells = nrow(result), samples = length(unique(result$sample)),
  domains = model$n_clusters, features = model$n_features,
  EM_iterations = model$iterations, converged = model$converged,
  mean_negative_log_likelihood = model$nll
)
```

# Spatial preservation

```{r spatial-map}
# A deterministic 40k-cell display keeps the HTML usable while retaining the
# spatial footprints of all sections.  Equal axes avoid geometry distortion.
set.seed(12345)
plot_idx <- sample.int(nrow(result), min(40000L, nrow(result)))
plot_df <- result[plot_idx, ]
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x, y, colour = r_domain)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.18, alpha = 0.60) + coord_equal() +
  facet_wrap(~sample, scales = "free") + scale_y_reverse() +
  labs(colour = "R domain", title = "Sample-local R Torch spatial domains") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9)
```

# Biological preservation

```{r cell-type-composition}
# Non-uniform cell-type composition is a necessary, but not sufficient,
# biological-preservation check.  It does not depend on permutation-sensitive
# GMM label numbers.
composition <- prop.table(table(result$r_domain, result$cell_type), margin = 1)
composition_long <- as.data.frame(composition)
names(composition_long) <- c("domain", "cell_type", "fraction")
ggplot(composition_long, aes(cell_type, domain, fill = fraction)) +
  geom_tile() + scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "R domain", fill = "Within-domain fraction",
       title = "Cell-type composition of R spatial domains") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 55, hjust = 1))
```

```{r top-enrichments}
do.call(rbind, lapply(split(composition_long, composition_long$domain), function(x) {
  head(x[order(x$fraction, decreasing = TRUE), ], 5)
}))
```

# Concordance with the official CellCharter domains

```{r official-label-concordance}
# The official cluster_20 labels are retained in the downloaded H5AD.  ARI is
# label-permutation invariant, but it is still not a measure of biological
# truth: different GMM starts or feature scaling can legitimately split/merge
# an official niche.
keep <- !is.na(result$official_cluster_20)
ari <- adjustedRandIndex(as.integer(result$r_domain[keep]),
                         as.integer(factor(result$official_cluster_20[keep])))
data.frame(adjusted_rand_index_against_official_cluster_20 = ari,
           note = "Method concordance only; assess it together with spatial footprints and cell-type enrichment.")
```

```{r domain-by-official-label}
tab <- prop.table(table(result$r_domain[keep], result$official_cluster_20[keep]), 1)
long <- as.data.frame(tab)
names(long) <- c("r_domain", "official_domain", "fraction")
ggplot(long, aes(official_domain, r_domain, fill = fraction)) + geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() + labs(x = "Official CellCharter domain", y = "R Torch domain",
                                 fill = "Within-R fraction") + theme_bw(base_size = 9)
```

# Verdict

Spatial preservation is supported when domains are anatomically coherent within
each physical section rather than forming cross-sample artefacts.  Biological
preservation is supported when those domains show reproducible, non-uniform
cell-type composition.  Concordance with `cluster_20` is useful sensitivity
analysis, not a pass/fail benchmark: a high ARI can still arise from a
biologically unhelpful partition, while a moderate ARI can reflect a defensible
change of domain resolution.
